title: Decide: Start Anyway or Delay
scenario: A hire has a blocked task the evening before start. Someone must decide: start anyway with a workaround, or delay the start. This is a governed judgement, not a gut call. Encode the decision and the rule that justifies it, so the same call is made the same way every time.
input: Hire H-4022, evening before start. Blocked task: hardware (laptop backordered). A loaner is available (a workaround). No critical task is blocked - accounts, access, and payroll are all done. Governed rule: START ANYWAY when the only blocks are non-critical AND a workaround exists; DELAY when a critical task (accounts, access, or payroll) is blocked with no workaround. Encode the decision.
instructions: Record whether a critical task is blocked (accounts, access, or payroll).
Record whether a workaround is available.
Apply the rule to set the decision (start-anyway or delay).
Return one JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Encode the degraded-mode decision: blockedTask hardware, criticalBlocked false (accounts/access/payroll are done), workaroundAvailable true (loaner), so decision start-anyway per the governed rule.
successMessage: Decision governed. A non-critical block with a workaround means start anyway - and the rule says why.
editorHelper: Apply the rule - the decision must follow from the inputs.

sections.title: Not every block delays a start
sections.body: A missing laptop with a loaner on hand should not cost someone their start date. A missing payroll enrollment might. The difference is what critical means - and the rule makes it explicit.

sections.title: Critical vs non-critical
sections.body: Accounts, access, and payroll gate the hire's ability to work and be paid - critical. Hardware has workarounds. Naming which blocks are critical is what turns a judgement into a repeatable rule.

sections.title: The decision must follow the rule
sections.body: Given non-critical block plus a workaround, the answer is start-anyway - every time, for every reviewer. A governed decision removes the coin-flip and the favoritism.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A decision record whose value is entailed by its inputs and the rule - auditable, consistent, defensible.

takeaway.heading: Decision governed
points: You encoded a start-vs-delay decision from an explicit rule.
Critical (accounts/access/payroll) versus non-critical made the call clear.
A non-critical block with a workaround means start-anyway - consistently.
The decision follows from its inputs, so it is auditable and fair.
The workflow can now make the hardest call the same way every time.
